gdp_level.source: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CN · GDP at current prices, sol million, annual, from 1991.
gdp_level.description: The total value of everything Peru produces in a year, at current prices. Shown from 1991, when the sol replaced the inti; the World Bank restates earlier years in today's soles, where they round to nothing.
gdp_level.real: “Make it real” swaps this to the Central Reserve Bank of Peru's real GDP, in soles at 2007 prices, quarterly, rolled into years. This strips out the effect of price changes, so it shows genuine output growth rather than growth that's really just inflation.
gdp_level.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each year at its own PEN/USD rate (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF, annual average), from 1991.

gdp_real.source: Central Reserve Bank of Peru (BCRP), series PN02538AQ · GDP by expenditure, sol million at 2007 prices, not seasonally adjusted, quarterly.
gdp_real.description: GDP adjusted for inflation, so changes reflect real output growth rather than price changes. Quarterly, from 1980.
gdp_real.real: This IS the “Make it real” series, toggling it off shows GDP at current prices (annual) instead.
gdp_real.dollar: With “Make it real” on, “Dollarise” converts every year at one rate, the average for the latest year, so dollar growth equals real growth.

gdp_growth_yoy.source: Central Reserve Bank of Peru (BCRP), series PN02507AQ · real GDP, change on the same quarter a year earlier, as published, to one decimal place.
gdp_growth_yoy.description: How much bigger or smaller the economy is than a year earlier, adjusted for inflation. Peru's quarterly GDP is not seasonally adjusted, so quarters are compared with the same quarter a year before.
gdp_growth_yoy.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic, converting the underlying soles to dollars doesn't change the percentage change. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

gdp_growth.source: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.KN · change in real GDP on the previous year, to one decimal place.
gdp_growth.description: How much the economy grew or shrank compared with the previous year, in real terms.
gdp_growth.real: This is already a real (inflation-adjusted) growth rate, “Make it real” has no additional effect on it.
gdp_growth.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic, converting the underlying soles to dollars doesn't change the percentage change. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

cpi.source: Central Reserve Bank of Peru (BCRP), series PN01273PM, from INEI · Metropolitan Lima consumer price index, all items, change on the same month a year earlier, to one decimal place, monthly.
cpi.description: How much consumer prices are rising compared with a year ago. Metropolitan Lima's index is Peru's headline inflation measure, the one the central bank targets at 1% to 3%.

cpi_mom.source: Central Reserve Bank of Peru (BCRP), series PN01271PM, from INEI · Metropolitan Lima consumer price index, all items, change on the previous month, not seasonally adjusted, to one decimal place.
cpi_mom.description: How much consumer prices changed in the latest month.

policy_rate.source: BIS central bank policy rates (WS_CBPOL, M.PE, extended with the daily series D.PE) · the Central Reserve Bank of Peru's reference rate, end of month, from September 2003; the current month shows the latest rate.
policy_rate.description: The reference rate, the interest rate the Central Reserve Bank of Peru sets to steer borrowing costs. The history starts in September 2003, when it became the bank's policy instrument.

unemployment.source: World Bank SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS · International Labour Organization modelled estimate, % of the labour force, annual.
unemployment.description: The share of the labour force that wants a job and is actively looking, but can't find one. This is the ILO's modelled estimate, not the statistics office's own survey rate.

exports.source: Central Reserve Bank of Peru (BCRP), series PN38714BM · exports of goods, free on board, US$ converted to soles at the BIS monthly average rate, monthly.
exports.description: The value of goods Peru sells to the rest of the world each month, in soles.
exports.dollar: BCRP's trade figures are in US dollars; the soles shown are converted at each month's BIS average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back at that year's World Bank rate.

imports.source: Central Reserve Bank of Peru (BCRP), series PN38718BM · imports of goods, free on board, US$ converted to soles at the BIS monthly average rate, monthly.
imports.description: The value of goods Peru buys from the rest of the world each month, in soles.
imports.dollar: BCRP's trade figures are in US dollars; the soles shown are converted at each month's BIS average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back at that year's World Bank rate.

trade_balance.source: Central Reserve Bank of Peru (BCRP) trade balance · exports less imports, both free on board, converted to soles at the BIS monthly average rate, monthly.
trade_balance.description: Exports minus imports of goods. A negative number is a trade deficit.
trade_balance.dollar: BCRP's trade figures are in US dollars; the soles shown are converted at each month's BIS average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back at that year's World Bank rate.

debt_gdp.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (GGXWDG_NGDP) · general government gross debt, % of GDP, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
debt_gdp.description: Everything government owes, across all levels of government, compared with the size of the economy.
debt_gdp.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

deficit.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (GGXCNL_NGDP) · general government net lending (+) or borrowing (-), % of GDP, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
deficit.description: The gap between what government takes in and what it spends in a year, across all levels of government. A negative number is a deficit.
deficit.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

current_account.source: World Bank BN.CAB.XOKA.GD.ZS · current account balance, % of GDP, annual.
current_account.description: The balance of trade in goods and services plus income and transfers with the rest of the world. A negative number means the country is borrowing from abroad.
current_account.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

fdi.source: World Bank BX.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS · foreign direct investment, net inflows, % of GDP, annual.
fdi.description: Long-term investment into the country by foreign companies and investors, such as building factories or buying a lasting stake in a business.
fdi.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

fx_usd.source: World Bank series PA.NUS.FCRF · official exchange rate, annual average, shown as US$ per S/1 (1 ÷ the published PEN per US$), from 1991.
fx_usd.description: How many US dollars one sol buys. A rising number means a stronger sol.
